variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: ML data pipeline design is the work of turning raw business events into trustworthy training examples and serving-time features. It matters because a model can appear healthy while learning from the wrong past or receiving different inputs in production.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Generate features once, then test offline and online parity”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Offline feature view
pairs.detail: Build historical rows as of each prediction timestamp.
pairs.explanation: Build historical rows as of each prediction timestamp. Point-in-time joins prevent labels and future events from leaking backward.

pairs.label: Online feature view
pairs.detail: Retrieve the latest eligible values under a bounded latency budget.
pairs.explanation: Retrieve the latest eligible values under a bounded latency budget. Record feature version and freshness with each prediction.

pairs.label: Parity test
pairs.detail: Replay representative events through both paths and compare values, defaults, windows, and entity coverage before promotion.
pairs.explanation: Replay representative events through both paths and compare values, defaults, windows, and entity coverage before promotion.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: ML data pipeline design is the work of turning raw business events into trustworthy training examples and serving-time features. It matters because a model can appear healthy while learning from the wrong past or receiving different inputs in production.
variants.prompt: What invariant protects an ML system from silent training-serving mismatch?
options: Training and serving consume data with explicit lineage, time semantics, and reproducible transformations
Every feature is recomputed from scratch for each request
Every event is processed by a streaming engine
Training uses the largest possible historical table
variants.explanation: The invariant makes a feature traceable, reconstructible, and comparable across offline and online consumers. The implementation can still be batch, streaming, or hybrid.
